$description: The DTCG single-source design tokens (UI-Architecture §3, D42). Values seed from the design handoff's Hearth OKLCH ramp + Ember accent + Geist (UI-Architecture §4.1 — ONLY the palette survives the seed). Everything downstream (src/styles/theme.css @theme block + src/tokens/index.ts typed map) is DERIVED by tokens.build.ts — never hand-authored; tests/ui/tokens enforces freshness.

background.$description: near-neutral charcoal (chroma ~0.006 @ hue 60) so the ONE Ember reads as intentional — UIP-101

surface-raised.$description: the elevation-RAMP mid panel tone (D44 §12.1 appearance.elevation=ramp) — a perceptible step between --color-sidebar (0.132, rail) and --color-card (0.205), so LIST/CONTEXT panels lift off the rail. Unused by the default flat composition; consumed only by shell.css `.shell-grid[data-elevation=ramp]`.

popover-foreground.$description: ONE white. It was a hand-authored oklch(0.96 0.004 75) — 0.005 lighter than --color-foreground for no stated reason, which rendered as two near-identical whites on one surface (a Select's popup value vs the labels beside it; preset typography census, 2026-08-02). The token stays SEMANTIC (a theme may still retint text-on-popover); only the unjustified drift in the base ramp goes.

primary.$description: Ember — the ONE signature accent (richer, glowing — UIP-101)

secondary.$description: ONE low-emphasis neutral surface — the same de-drift as popover-foreground/accent-foreground. It was a hand-authored oklch(0.255 0.007 60) against muted's oklch(0.255 0.006 60): identical lightness and hue, 0.001 chroma apart (Oklab ΔE 0.0010), i.e. the same colour spelled twice (near-duplicate lint, 2026-08-02). muted holds the literal because it is the more-consumed of the two (83 utility sites vs 35), so the collapse moves the fewest pixels. The token stays SEMANTIC — every seed value-set re-values secondary and muted independently, and a theme may still separate them.

muted-foreground.$description: secondary/placeholder text — AA on every Hearth surface incl. the input fill (worst ≈4.9:1 over input-on-popover; the prior 0.705 was 4.29:1 there — a marginal AA miss). Custom themes derive this via theme-scope/clamp mutedForegroundOn.

accent-foreground.$description: ONE white — the same de-drift as popover-foreground above (was oklch(0.96 0.004 75); a selected/highlighted row's text must not be a second white beside the unselected rows it sits with).

destructive.$description: POLARITY-AWARE via CSS light-dark() (arg order is light-arm FIRST, dark-arm second): ONE static semantic token with two hand-tuned arms selected by the inherited color-scheme (base :root dark, [data-theme=light] flips to light). A single static red physically cannot clear AA-NORMAL 4.5:1 as text on BOTH a near-black chrome and a near-white card — so the dark arm (oklch(0.65 0.19 25), the original value, byte-identical Hearth/Mocha render) is a bright red that clears on dark surfaces (5.07:1 card, 4.59:1 popover), and the light arm (oklch(0.50 0.19 25)) is a deeper red that clears on the light seed's card/popover at 6.54:1. Paired with the destructive-foreground below it also clears AA-NORMAL as a solid `bg-destructive` pill in each polarity (dark 5.15:1, light 6.24:1). The bright/dark-foreground convention matches the rest of the accent family.

destructive-foreground.$description: POLARITY-AWARE light-dark() (light arm first): text on the solid `bg-destructive` pill. Dark arm (oklch(0.2 0.03 25), the original) is DARK text on the bright dark-scheme red (5.15:1); the light arm (oklch(0.98 0.01 25)) is near-white text on the deeper light-scheme red (6.24:1) — the light red is dark enough to take a light foreground, the opposite polarity from dark. Only ever sits on `bg-destructive`, never a neutral surface.

success.$description: POLARITY-AWARE light-dark() (light arm first): the success/confirm green. Dark arm (oklch(0.72 0.13 155), the original) clears AA as `text-success` on dark chrome; the light arm (oklch(0.47 0.12 155)) is a deeper green clearing 6.32:1 as text on the light seed's card, and 5.90:1 as a solid pill under the light success-foreground below.

success-foreground.$description: POLARITY-AWARE light-dark() (light arm first): text on the solid `bg-success` pill. Dark arm (oklch(0.14 0.02 150), the original) is dark text on the bright dark-scheme green; the light arm (oklch(0.97 0.01 150)) is near-white text on the deeper light-scheme green (5.90:1).

warning.$description: the partial/caution intent (rpg check bands, staleness). POLARITY-AWARE light-dark() (light arm first): dark arm (oklch(0.79 0.13 75), the original) is the bright amber for dark chrome; the light arm (oklch(0.50 0.11 75)) is a deeper amber clearing 6.03:1 as text on the light seed's card, and 5.77:1 as a solid pill under the light warning-foreground below.

warning-foreground.$description: POLARITY-AWARE light-dark() (light arm first): text on the solid `bg-warning` pill. Dark arm (oklch(0.2 0.03 85), the original) is dark text on the bright dark-scheme amber; the light arm (oklch(0.98 0.01 85)) is near-white text on the deeper light-scheme amber (5.77:1).

info.$description: informational intent (UIP-101 new token; mockup .theme-hearth --info). POLARITY-AWARE light-dark() (light arm first): dark arm (oklch(0.7 0.1 232), the original W2 value) is the bright blue for dark chrome; the light arm (oklch(0.48 0.1 232)) is a deeper blue clearing 6.29:1 as text on the light seed's card. Paired with the info-foreground below it also clears AA-NORMAL as a solid `bg-info` pill in each polarity (north-star PP1 minted the foreground; per-palette pill-swept). Arms are written in browser-round-trip form (no trailing zeros) so the badge CT's `toHaveCSS(resolvedTokenColor)` matches the computed style — same color as W2's `0.70 0.10`.

info-foreground.$description: POLARITY-AWARE light-dark() (light arm first; D71 static intent token, north-star PP1): text on the solid `bg-info` pill. Dark arm (oklch(0.2 0.03 232)) is dark text on the bright dark-scheme blue (6.90:1); the light arm (oklch(0.98 0.01 232)) is near-white text on the deeper light-scheme blue (6.03:1). Mirrors the success/warning foreground shape (bright bg → dark fg on dark scheme, deeper bg → near-white fg on light scheme). Only ever sits on `bg-info`, never a neutral surface.

highlight.$description: text-mark / search-match highlight — a bright, more-yellow highlighter tone, deliberately distinct from warning's caution amber. POLARITY-INDEPENDENT: unlike the 4 divergent intents (destructive/success/warning/info) this is ONE plain value, NOT a light-dark() pair — a saturated yellow mark reads on both a black and a white page, and highlight is a BACKGROUND (never rendered as text), so the only AA constraint is the dark highlight-foreground on it (9.98:1). The former light-dark(X,X) was a literal no-op (both arms identical) that implied two tuned arms; collapsed to the single value it always resolved to (derive-modernization-audit §W6 cleanup).

highlight-foreground.$description: POLARITY-INDEPENDENT (a single plain value, mirroring highlight — not a light-dark() pair): dark text on the `bg-highlight` mark, 9.98:1. The highlight mark is the same saturated yellow on both pages, so the foreground stays the one dark tone; the former no-op light-dark(X,X) was collapsed (derive-modernization-audit §W6).

sidebar.$description: deeper than content — the RAIL/LIST chrome

backdrop.$description: the polarity-FIXED dimming smoke — modal/drawer/select backdrops, the shell dismiss scrim, the wallpaper-dim layer, and both text-shadow halos (shell over-photo + wordmark; owner fence 2026-08-18: every already-correct scrim job keeps this exact value, byte-identical across the rename) (D43 §11.4 — never bg-black/50). Dimming means darker BY DESIGN, in every palette (the light seed deliberately keeps a dark smoke). It was `--color-scrim`, retired at #204: that one name also served as the transcript's over-art READING plate, whose polarity must FOLLOW the palette — one token cannot be a fixed dimmer and a polarity-following plate, and the overloaded name is how the bug was born (the photo-backing author reached for the token literally named scrim). A text PLATE over art rides color.reading-plate, never this.

reading-plate.$description: the transcript's over-art text backing (#204) — DERIVED, never designed: background + THEME_DERIVATION.readingPlate.deltaL (−0.038) at .alpha (0.65), so the plate always carries the palette's own polarity and the palette's inks land on their own surface. This literal must equal that derivation off color.background (pinned by palette-contrast.suite.test.ts, which also proves the alpha floors AA for the derived foreground over worst-case art); ThemeScope emits the same derivation for custom/carried themes. NOT color.backdrop (the fixed smoke): a token names ONE polarity semantic.

reading-band.$description: the sticky attribution BAND (#241, owner-ruled off #223) — the reading plate's colour at alpha 1, and nothing else. The band pins a tall turn's speaker name over the turn's OWN prose, so it must occlude (#168's opacity ruling, untouched here) — but it shipped as color.card (base +0.047) while the prose beneath rides the plate (base -0.038), and that constant DL read as an unintentional step, two stacked tones per message. Deriving it from the plate kills the step by construction: this literal must equal derive(background) per THEME_DERIVATION.readingPlate at READING_BAND_ALPHA (kit/theme-derivation readingBandSurface), pinned by palette-contrast.suite.test.ts, and ThemeScope emits the same derivation for custom/carried themes. It pairs with color.foreground (the base's derived ink), NOT card-foreground: the band is no longer a ramp member.

sheen.$description: POLARITY-FIXED sheen highlight — the deliberate white gloss at the FOOT of a gradient-border glow (the CTA ring, the active tab, the active rail button), where the head is the theme's own --color-primary. Opaque here; each site applies its own alpha through the relative-color form `oklch(from var(--color-sheen) l c h / 0.0N)`, so the three tuned alphas (0.04/0.02/0.03) stay per-site while the HUE is one decision. It was three bare `oklch(1 0 0 / 0.0N)` literals sitting beside token-derived halves — invisible to every theme, including a light one where a white gloss is a no-op. A theme that wants a polarity-aware gloss overrides this var; the seed value-sets do NOT carry it (no per-theme variance today, and they are restricted to the ThemeScope-emitted class + color.backdrop).

shadow-hairline.$description: the ELEVATION INGREDIENT: the 1px edge-light ring of shadow.overlay. Polarity-FOLLOWING, and it is why this exists as a colour token at all (#232): Tailwind v4 INLINES a `--shadow-*` @theme value into the `.shadow-*` utility at build time, so a `[data-theme]` override of --shadow-overlay is a no-op for every consumer that uses the utility — a var() INGREDIENT survives the inlining and resolves at runtime. On a dark plate the ring is white-alpha edge light; on a light plate a white hairline is invisible (measured 1.29:1 against the page) and the ring must be a dark alpha instead, which is what the light value-set carries.

shadow-highlight.$description: the ELEVATION INGREDIENT: shadow.overlay's inset top-highlight (the light-from-above cue). Polarity-FOLLOWING for the same reason as shadow-hairline; a light palette spends its elevation budget on the ring instead, because a white top-highlight on a near-white card paints nothing.

shadow-ambient-near.$description: the ELEVATION INGREDIENT: shadow.overlay's tight CONTACT shadow (0 2px 4px). Carries its own alpha, because the alpha IS the per-polarity decision — a dark UI's float earns a heavy near-black contact layer, a light one reads as a torn-out sticker at the same value (home-delta 2026-08-18).

shadow-ambient-far.$description: the ELEVATION INGREDIENT: shadow.overlay's deep AMBIENT drop (0 12px 32px) — the loudest layer, and the one that threw a visible halo ~14px past the card box under the Light seed while it still wore this dark recipe. Alpha per polarity, same as shadow-ambient-near.

shadow-cta-highlight.$description: the ELEVATION INGREDIENT: the primary CTA's inset top-highlight (shadow.cta / shadow.cta-glow). Distinct from shadow-highlight because it catches on the PRIMARY fill, not on a surface — the light seed's darker primary takes a slightly stronger catch.

chart-1.$description: Chart ramp step 1 (ember) — polarity-aware categorical fill. The dark arm is the original value byte-identical; the darker light arm clears WCAG 1.4.11 against every legal light chart host while the five hues remain mutually distinguishable.

chart-2.$description: Chart ramp step 2 (muted teal) — polarity-aware; dark arm byte-identical. See chart-1.

chart-3.$description: Chart ramp step 3 (dusty violet) — polarity-aware; dark arm byte-identical. See chart-1.

chart-4.$description: Chart ramp step 4 (sage) — polarity-aware; dark arm byte-identical. See chart-1.

chart-5.$description: Chart ramp step 5 (clay) — polarity-aware; dark arm byte-identical. See chart-1.

track-1.$description: D71 track ramp step 1 (Context-Panel-Program §4.8) — a 6-step CATEGORICAL ramp for pool/meter/clock FILLS in the tracker block kit; also serves future charts. Pools are user-defined data and need a stable categorical color, assigned by definition order. NOW POLARITY-AWARE `light-dark(<light-arm>, <dark-arm>)` (the divergent-intent shape, not the plain chart-* value): the RULING SURVIVED, its INPUT changed (#697). The old ruling (a single mid-L value; 'a fill is never rendered as text so the value TEXT beside it carries meaning') is superseded — the gauge FILL is itself a non-text UI component under WCAG 1.4.11, and at mid-L these steps rendered 1.89–2.65:1 against the LIGHT panel (sidebar/surface-raised), below the 3:1 minimum, while measuring 5.9–9.3:1 on dark. The DARK arm is byte-identical to the original ramp (dark render unchanged); the LIGHT arm darkens each hue (keeping hue, keeping chroma where the sRGB gamut allows) to clear ≥3:1 against every light backing (panels + the bg-input rail composited over them, worse of float+8bit), while the 6 hues stay mutually distinguishable — the categorical mechanism is intact, only the light polarity is retuned. The active arm follows color-scheme (base :root dark, [data-theme=light] flips to light; the clamp derives it for custom themes, the intent-token precedent). Base-only (NOT in THEME_SCOPE_EMIT_VARS); any seed theme json MAY still override. Dark arm = the v2 mockup stand-in (--track-1, vitality green).

track-2.$description: D71 track ramp step 2 (resolve blue) — polarity-aware light arm to clear 1.4.11 on the light panel, dark arm byte-identical; see track-1.

track-3.$description: D71 track ramp step 3 (supply gold) — light arm at c 0.11 (one gamut step under the dark arm's 0.12 at this lower L); see track-1.

track-4.$description: D71 track ramp step 4 (corruption violet) — see track-1.

track-5.$description: D71 track ramp step 5 (rose) — see track-1.

track-6.$description: D71 track ramp step 6 (teal) — light arm at c 0.09 (one gamut step under the dark arm's 0.10 at this lower L); see track-1.

sky-day.$description: ATMOSPHERIC set (Waystone, side-eye ROOT CAUSE 2026-08-01): a small dedicated sky palette, because the stone was painting its sky with the CATEGORICAL chart ramp (track-*) mixed toward --color-background — which inverted day/night on the Light seed (midnight rendered LIGHTER than noon). POLARITY-FIXED by design and base-only (the track-*/chart-* precedent: NOT in THEME_SCOPE_EMIT_VARS, no seed override): night is dark in every theme, because a night sky IS dark — the stone's CHROME (ring, bezel, horizon, text) stays theme-reactive, its SKY does not. sky-day = the daylight zenith.

sky-day-horizon.$description: ATMOSPHERIC — the pale band where a daylight sky meets the horizon (see sky-day).

sky-night.$description: ATMOSPHERIC — THE NIGHT ANCHOR (see sky-day). The one value the whole night half derives from; polarity-fixed dark so midnight can never render lighter than noon.

sky-night-horizon.$description: ATMOSPHERIC — the lighter band above a night horizon (see sky-day).

sky-ember.$description: ATMOSPHERIC — the golden-hour fire at dawn/dusk (see sky-day).

sky-ember-deep.$description: ATMOSPHERIC — the deep red band under a golden hour (see sky-day).

sky-twilight.$description: ATMOSPHERIC — the violet wedge between dusk and full night (see sky-day).

sky-star.$description: ATMOSPHERIC — starlight: the NIGHT ANCHOR's contrast partner, never --color-foreground (which flips dark on a light theme and turned the stars into dirt). See sky-day.

sky-cloud.$description: ATMOSPHERIC — a lit cloud deck (see sky-day).

sky-cloud-dark.$description: ATMOSPHERIC — a storm deck: DARKER than the lit one (they were inverted, so storm clouds were the brightest thing in the sky). See sky-day.

sky-rain.$description: ATMOSPHERIC — falling water: a desaturated blue-grey, not the categorical teal it used to borrow. See sky-day.

sky-ash.$description: ATMOSPHERIC — ashfall motes: dark grit (they were bright peach confetti). See sky-day.

dialogue.$description: amber-gold quoted speech — the ONE saturated prose voice on the warm-neutral page (chroma 0.10 vs narration 0.02); ST quote-amber lineage. Owner-picked 2026-07-31. Was {color.foreground} (a visual no-op). D44 §12.1 dialogueColor (D44 §12.1 dialogueColor)

micro.$description: 2px — the smallest intentional gap between a compact glyph and its caption. The shell mobile rail uses it between icon and label; it is below the 4px atom floor because the two pieces form one tab identity, not two neighbouring controls.

tight.$description: intent token — ATOM gaps inside an island (label↔bar, glyph↔text, value↔caption). UI-Density-Law.md §2.2/D2: the mocks' instrument internals cluster at 3–5px (`.meter` gap 3px, `.rel` gap 4px, `.chip` gap 4px), below `field`, so they either rounded up (visibly loose) or went raw (gate-red). 4px is the 4pt sub-grid floor. `field` (6px) deliberately STAYS 6px — with `tight` added it is the 2pt sub-step (Carbon spacing-01 precedent, D3).

field.$description: intent token — within a labeled field

row.$description: intent token — items in a row

block.$description: intent token — blocks in a stack

section.$description: intent token — sections in a surface

density-section-compact.$description: the compact arm of the section spacing intent. The other compact density arms reuse existing canonical spacing steps; this is the one value the scale did not already contain. Consumed only through the generated private density aliases in orb.cssValues.

touch-target.$description: the ≥44px touch floor — POINTER-CONDITIONAL (D62 P1, §4b axis 3): the 44px value holds by default (coarse/unknown pointers); fine pointers narrow it to 28px via the emitted @media(pointer:fine) override. gate touch-target-floor asserts the floor per-pointer.

control-sm.$description: control-height — POINTER-CONDITIONAL (D62 P1): 44px at coarse (meets the touch floor), 32px at fine via the @media(pointer:fine) override. The fine value is the design-audit tap-target hard floor (TAP_FAIL_PX=32, WCAG 2.5.8's 24px + repo margin) — it was 28px (Task #76: two side-eye passes + design-audit flagged every compact/icon control below the floor). compact density tightens via data-density, orthogonal to pointer.

avatar-sm.$description: avatar DISPLAY size — decoupled from control heights (§13.9 D62 delta): pointer-independent, never narrows. 24px — cast-bar overlap chips

avatar-hero.$description: 64px — the character-detail hero avatar (ux-flow-revamp J9). The display-only hero size L1 deferred to the surface lane that needed it; still pointer-independent (a display glyph, not a touch target), same as the sm/md/lg trio.

switch-track.$description: the Switch VISIBLE track WIDTH — POINTER-CONDITIONAL since #420: 64px at coarse, 48px at fine via the emitted @media(pointer:fine) override. It was pointer-INDEPENDENT at 48px until 2026-08-22, and that is precisely what broke: once the ROOT began carrying the ≥44px coarse floor on its HEIGHT (`pointer-coarse:h-touch-target`, 382e46d83) a 48-wide track around a 32px thumb became a 1.091-aspect near-circle with track painting on all four sides of the knob — side-eye #420 measured it and called it a crescent moon, not a switch, on every touch surface. The WIDTH now scales with the height so the control keeps a switch's silhouette (64x44, aspect 1.455) and the travel stays legible (travel = switch-track − switch-thumb, so 32px at coarse and 16px at fine, both auto-derived by the thumb's translate calc). The FINE arm is byte-identical to what it always was (48x32, travel 16) — #371's fine-pointer receipts hold unchanged.

switch-thumb.$description: 32px — the Switch track HEIGHT and (square) thumb size. Pointer-INDEPENDENT (pairs with switch-track); the thumb slides switch-track − switch-thumb (16px), an unambiguous on/off travel. Was 28px — raised to 32px (Task #76) so the Switch's own box clears the design-audit tap-target hard floor (TAP_FAIL_PX=32) on fine pointers, matching control-sm. TRUTH-REPAIRED 2026-08-22 (this clause used to say the ::before pseudo carries the ≥44px coarse hit floor): since 382e46d83 the ROOT grows to `h-touch-target` at a coarse pointer, so this token is the track height at a FINE pointer and the THUMB size at every pointer — the thumb deliberately stays 32px inside the 44px coarse track so its 16px travel stays legible.

checkbox.$description: 18px — the Checkbox/Radio VISIBLE box (display size, §13.9 family: pointer-INDEPENDENT like avatars/switch). Decoupled from --spacing-section (it previously rode size-section, coupling the box to the GROUP-GAP intent token — retuning section spacing resized every checkbox). The ≥44px coarse hit floor is carried by the ::before size-touch-target pseudo, never this box. PP5 (D66).

slider-thumb.$description: 24px — the Slider VISIBLE thumb (display size, §13.9 family: pointer-INDEPENDENT like avatars/switch-thumb/checkbox). Decoupled from --spacing-section (it previously rode size-section, the same GROUP-GAP coupling PP5 fixed for checkbox/radio — retuning section spacing resized every slider thumb; W2 flagged it, derive-modernization-audit §W5). The ≥44px drag/hit floor is carried separately by the h-control-sm control row, never this thumb. Its HALF is --spacing-slider-inset; the two move together.

slider-inset.$description: 12px — HALF of --spacing-slider-thumb, and the margin the Slider's Control carries on both inline sides. Base UI centres each thumb ON its value position (left: pct% of the Control's padding box, shifted -50%), so at min and max the thumb hangs half its width OUTSIDE the Control. Measured at a 430px coarse viewport (side-eye 2026-08-22 P2-8): a full-bleed row put the max thumb at x 406→430 and the min thumb at 0→24 — flush with the screen edge, with its grabbable half sitting on the OS edge-swipe bezel. Insetting the Control by half a thumb pulls both extremes back inside the row; the rail shortens by one thumb width and nothing else moves. This is a literal 0.75rem because token $values carry no calc — if slider-thumb changes, change this with it (its own description says so).

glyph-xs.$description: 16px — the SQUARE GLYPH-BUTTON box ramp (display size, §13.9 family: pointer-INDEPENDENT like avatars/switch-thumb/checkbox/slider-thumb). A glyph button is an icon-only micro-affordance that rides INSIDE a dense row (a badge's dismiss, a tracker row's delete) and must not claim a control height: at `control-sm` the delete on a 20px badge would be taller than the badge. Deliberately NOT the avatar ramp — an avatar is a portrait size, and coupling the two means retuning cast-bar chips resizes every delete button (the PP5 / slider-thumb lesson). The ≥ touch-floor hit area is carried by Button's `glyph-*` ::after touch-target pseudo, never this box. xs = the tightest step: a dismiss inside a `sm` Badge.

glyph-sm.$description: 20px — the glyph-button ramp's ROW step (pairs the family header): the trailing delete on a list row (quest, beat, pack item) and the RpgFieldLock pin. Holds a 12px `xs` Icon with a 4px optical surround.

glyph-md.$description: 24px — the glyph-button ramp's EDITOR step: an inline toolbar of icon toggles in a definition/editor row (band-visibility, story-lock, delete). Holds a 12px `xs` Icon with a 6px surround, and reads as a control without stealing the row's height.

glyph-lg.$description: 32px — the glyph-button ramp's PICKER step: a grid/strip of icon CHOICES where the glyph is the content being chosen (the pack icon picker), so it holds a 16px `sm` Icon and is the only step that also clears the fine-pointer tap floor on its own box.

inset.$description: 4px — SUB-CONTROL marks INSIDE a component: keycap, qty badge, segment tick, ghost socket, swatch. UI-Density-Law.md §2.1/D2: the approved mocks author 4–5px radii for exactly this class (`.artifact .abar button` 4px, `.choicebtn .k` 4px) with no token to land on. The step BELOW `control` (6px, anything you operate).

portrait-width.$description: Portable numerator for the portrait aspect ratio.

portrait-height.$description: Portable denominator for the portrait aspect ratio.

banner-width.$description: Portable numerator for the banner aspect ratio.

banner-height.$description: Portable denominator for the banner aspect ratio.

dimension.$description: STRUCTURAL shell geometry (rail/chrome/panel) — the app-shell's private layout constants, promoted from raw shell.css literals into the DTCG source so nothing visual bypasses a token (WS0). These are NOT themeable (a theme is a value-set, never a structural mode — §4.1/§12.1); the css-structure test asserts shell.css consumes ONLY var(--dimension-*) for geometry. Not a Tailwind utility namespace — consumed via raw var(--dimension-*) in the one shell-tier CSS file.

shell-accent-edge.$description: the shell frame's hairline-plus accent edge: the active rail marker's thickness/end-cap and the docked context band's inset binding. One shell geometry decision, never a theme value.

shell-title-floor-ch.$description: portable character-count input for the topbar title's minimum visible text floor; serialized as ch by orb.cssValues.

shell-notice-cap.$description: portable absolute arm of the shell notice band's normal-flow height budget; combined with the viewport arm by orb.cssValues.

shell-notice-viewport-cap.$description: portable dynamic-viewport percentage input for the shell notice band's height budget; serialized as dvh by orb.cssValues.

rail.$description: the persistent thin icon-rail width (~56px, §4.1). Also the mobile bottom-tab-bar height.

chrome-row.$description: topbar + panel-header height — the chrome row (~48px). Was a bare 3rem literal duplicated 4× in shell.css.

panel-floor.$description: the RESPONSIVE FLOOR both side-panel clamps share — the narrowest a docked panel may ever be, and (since #242) the floor the conditional both-docked squeeze may not push the LIST panel past. Its own token because three sites must agree on one number: the two clamps below reference it, and shell.css's squeeze needs it as a bare value (a max() operand cannot read the floor back out of a clamp()).

panel-context-step.$description: the CONTEXT pane's SQUEEZE FLOOR (#242) — and it is an owner ruling, not a taste pick: 660b2dd4 widened panel-context to 30vw precisely so a STANDARD 1280px desktop reaches 384px — the 24rem container step where the Waystone paints at its focal 120px. The #242 both-docked squeeze therefore takes its slack from the LIST pane first and stops at this step on the context side, rather than trading the rpg takeover's focal stone for reading width. Where the deficit outlives both floors the content track stays short — a shell-grid limit, stated, not faked.

content-reading-floor.$description: 640px — the CONTENT track width at which the transcript's REAL-CHARACTER reading floor is met (#242, owner-ruled off #240). Measured, not designed: at viewport 1360 / both panels docked the content track is 569.6px and the room's own prose renders 55.3 real characters per line; the recovery needed to reach 65 is +70px, measured in the CT against the transcript's actual glyphs (chat-room-track.suite.ct.tsx — the ruling's sketched +60 lands at 63.7 chars, 9.6px short, so the target is honoured rather than the estimate). The owner ruled this REAL-CHARACTER floor over the token-strict 65ch one (which needs ~+96px and would cost far more panel). Consumed ONLY by shell.css's conditional squeeze as the threshold — above it nothing moves, so a viewport where the floor already fits is byte-identical. In rem so it tracks appearance.fontScale, exactly like the ch-based measure it stands in for.

shell-breakpoint.$description: the ONE viewport breakpoint (desktop⇄mobile, §4b axis 2). CANNOT be consumed via var() in @media — shell.css keeps the 48rem literal; this token exists so a test asserts the CSS literal + the use-is-mobile-viewport.ts matchMedia twin agree.

panel-fluid.$description: Portable viewport-width coefficient for the primary panel clamp.

panel-cap.$description: Portable maximum for the primary panel clamp.

panel-context-fluid.$description: Portable viewport-width coefficient for the context panel clamp.

panel-context-cap.$description: Portable maximum for the context panel clamp.

prose.$description: WS3 D44 §12.1 appearance.shadowEffects — the layered readability halo on message PROSE only (never chrome). OKLCH-black form of the researched recipe (0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.45), 0 0 6px rgba(0,0,0,.25)) so the literal survives the no-color-literals gate; consumed as `text-shadow`, not `box-shadow` (Style Dictionary emits the raw value either way — the CSS property choice lives at the call site, [data-shadow] in globals.css).

blur.$description: WS3 D44 §12.1 appearance.blurSurfaces — the FULL glass recipe (4 ingredients: backdrop-filter blur+saturate here, the translucent surface fill here, the existing --color-border hairline as the edge, the [data-blur-*] gate in globals.css). NOT naive blur.

strength.$description: backdrop-filter blur radius — the researched recipe's ~14px.

fill-chrome.$description: the translucent surface-fill mix percentage for PURE CHROME surfaces (panels/composer/modals) — `color-mix(in oklab, var(--color-surface) 70%, transparent)`. The Reading-Surface rule (Marinara steal): chrome gets a LIGHTER fill than text-heavy surfaces.

fill-dense.$description: the translucent surface-fill mix percentage for TEXT-HEAVY surfaces (messages, when opted in) — more opaque than fill-chrome so scrolling prose stays legible over the blur (Marinara's variable-glass-opacity steal).

saturate.$description: the glass recipe's backdrop saturation boost — the 4th ingredient beside strength/fill-chrome/fill-dense; consumed as saturate(var(--blur-saturate)) at every backdrop-filter site.

immersive.$description: Phase 4 §B.2 chatStyle immersive-mode geometry (FINAL-Persona-and-Immersive-Chat-Visuals.md), REDONE for readability (the reading-surface rule — art fades to a clean surface BEFORE the text, never under it) — the per-mode avatar/decoration dimensions for Echo/Whisper/Hush/Ripple, tokenized so no magic px/%/hex lands in message-row-variants.ts (§B.6 'no hardcoded magic numbers'). Tide's per-paragraph train gap reuses the existing spacing.field intent token — no new geometry needed there.

echo-art-width.$description: Echo: the ART PANE's own width — a FIXED column beside the prose, never a percentage of the bubble (#212). It was `echo-feather: 55%`, spent as the bubble's `padding-right` inside a `max-w-prose` box: 55% of 558px is 307px of padding, so the reading line rendered 239px = 28 characters against the house 65-75ch law, and the same percentage made the art box grow with the message (a 400x600 portrait painted into a 558x2965 `cover` box = a 4.94x upscale cropped past the subject's head). Now the art sits OUTSIDE the measure: the bubble's max-width is `65ch + this` (the prose measure is untouched), the padding on the art side is exactly this width, the feather gradient's stop is this width, and the art layer is painted at `this auto` anchored to its top outer corner — so the portrait is DOWN-scaled from its 400px request and the subject stays in frame at any message length. Consumed by message-row-variants.ts (both echo arms) and by the no-avatar edge tile in message-row-bubble.tsx, which must be pixel-identical to the with-art pane.

whisper-feather.$description: Whisper: the gradient stop (of `whisper-banner-height`, the band's own box) where the art fully dissolves into the bubble's own bg color, softening the band→text transition.

stripe-width.$description: 3px — the theme-color (--color-speaker) accent-stripe thickness: Whisper's top stripe, Hush's left stripe.

ripple-portrait-width.$description: 180px — the Ripple VN sticky-portrait's fixed width (height derives from the 2:3 aspect.portrait ratio). Ripple ignores the avatarSize/avatarShape user prefs by design (§B.2/§B.3 documented VN shape override).

reading.$description: Phase 4b §B.5.3 granular reading-typography (FINAL-Persona-and-Immersive-Chat-Visuals.md) — the STARTING values the appearance.readingLineHeight/readingLetterSpacing/readingParagraphSpacing sliders resolve to (the contracts schema default/catch mirrors these exactly, so a fresh user's message render is byte-identical to pre-4b). Root-var-overridden per user via useAppearanceRootEffects; consumed on [data-slot="message-bubble"]. THE READING-SURFACE RULE: this group governs spacing/sizing only — blur/glow never land on the reading surface.

line-height.$description: mirrors leading.body — the message-bubble prose baseline

paragraph-spacing.$description: gap between paragraphs inside one message bubble — mirrors spacing.block

measure-ch.$description: Portable character-count decision for the reading measure.

measure-min-ch.$description: Portable character-count decision for the minimum reading measure.

fade.$description: Phase 4b §B.5b polish — the chat-list edge-fade (a mask-image gradient on the thread scroll container, softly dissolving messages under the header/composer instead of hard-clipping). Token-driven so the fade distance isn't a magic number in globals.css.

edge-stop.$description: the mask-image gradient stop (of the scroll container's own height, from each edge) where content is fully opaque again.

border-width.$description: Phase 4b §B.5b polish — border-width tokens outside the radius/color families above.

hairline.$description: the avatar hairline border (auto-on when a background image is active, [data-has-bg-image]) — keeps an avatar from dissolving into a blurred/photo background. Consumed via var(--border-width-hairline), never a raw arbitrary border width.

control.$description: the STRUCTURAL border a control root paints (the Switch track today) — minted at #424 because a border-box root's border is ARITHMETIC, not just paint: the Switch's content box is 2× this narrower than --spacing-switch-track, and the thumb's travel calc must subtract it or the checked knob lands one border-width proud of the right rim (measured insetRight −1 at both pointers). The root spells its width from this same token, so the geometry and the paint can never drift apart. Consumed via var(--border-width-control), never a raw 1px.

micro.$description: 10.5px — the micro-caps section-label voice (UIP-103); pair with tracking.micro + weight 600 + uppercase

none.$description: single-line glyph-caption leading with no extra line box; used by shell rail labels.

micro-em.$description: Portable numeric decision serialized as em for the micro-label tracking.

cq-sm.$description: container-breakpoint scale (UI-Architecture §3) — @container queries use these, never raw widths (gate no-raw-container-widths)

dialog-sm.$description: modal chrome width — 400px (D62 UIP-401, Dialog size=sm). DISTINCT concept from container.cq-* (those are @container breakpoints, not modal widths — one-home rule). Consumed via max-w-(--width-dialog-sm), never a raw bracket (gate no-arbitrary-tw-values).

dialog-lg.$description: 720px — the wide Dialog (Dialog size=lg; settings-adjacent surfaces)

dialog-xl.$description: 1040px — the large shell modal (Dialog size=xl): settings + other nav-plus-content modals. Fills most of the viewport (h-full inside a gutter-padded, blurred backdrop) but stays a centered card, not full-bleed. Consumed via max-w-(--width-dialog-xl).

sidebar-sm.$description: 220px — the settings overlay's left category-nav column (D62 J11). A fixed in-modal nav rail; consumed via w-(--width-sidebar-sm), never a raw bracket (gate no-arbitrary-tw-values). DISTINCT from the shell RAIL (--rail-w, 56px) and the panel tracks (--panel-w).

control-col.$description: 200px — the RIGHT control column of a horizontal settings row (UIP-404): label+description left, control docked right in this fixed column so every row's control aligns and a select can't stretch to 100%. Consumed via w-(--width-control-col) by @orb/ui Field (orientation=horizontal) + SettingRow; never a raw bracket (gate no-arbitrary-tw-values).

label-col.$description: 152px — the LEFT label column of an instrument knob row (the preset params deck's KnobRow, preset-surface-redesign.md §4.1): the mirror of width.control-col, sized so a column of knob labels reads down one edge while the slider keeps the middle. DISTINCT from control-col (that is the settings row's RIGHT control dock, and a knob row's control is the flexing track, not a fixed column). Consumed via w-(--width-label-col); never a raw bracket (gate no-arbitrary-tw-values).

content-col.$description: 720px — the MEASURE cap for an editor's CONTENT column (the preset editor's five views; the width every preset-redesign mock draws its content panel at). A pane wider than this stretched knob rows to ~840px with a ~60% dead gutter and ran explanatory glosses to ~130ch against the 65-75ch reading measure (side-eye F-16, 2026-08-02). The column is CENTERED (mx-auto — the character editor's own convention) and breathes to width.content-col-wide once its container clears @5xl. Consumed via max-w-(--width-content-col); never a raw bracket (gate no-arbitrary-tw-values).

content-col-wide.$description: 896px — the BREATHE step of width.content-col, applied only once the content pane itself clears the @5xl container breakpoint (i.e. panels collapsed / focus mode). A fixed 720 clamp inside a ~1520px pane left ~800px of dead void (owner, 2026-08-02: 'looks okay when both panels are out, but when you close them it looks awful'). 56rem keeps explanatory glosses inside the ~65-75ch reading measure at the deck's 13px step while the knob rows stop looking marooned. Consumed via @5xl:max-w-(--width-content-col-wide); never a raw bracket (gate no-arbitrary-tw-values).

number-inline.$description: 80px — the box of the INLINE numeric twin (NumberField size=inline, preset-surface-redesign.md §13): a stepper-less mono field sitting beside a slider in a knob row. Sized to hold the widest datum the deck feeds it (a grouped 6-digit context window, "131,072") at the `code` type step plus its padding, so a column of knob rows aligns on one number edge. Consumed by @orb/ui NumberField's size axis; never a raw bracket (gate no-arbitrary-tw-values).

toast.$description: ABOVE popover (was 60, below it). MEASURED occlusion: the notifications popover (positioner z-65, box y49-98 x984-1266) covered the toast stack (z-60, y48-96 x896-1280) by 272x26px INCLUDING its close button, so the toast could neither be read nor dismissed — a collision created when the stack moved top-right. Ruled on D41's degraded-and-loud posture: a warning toast that slides under chrome and auto-dismisses unseen (5-12s) re-creates the exact silent-degrade class the warning channel exists to kill, and that failure is TOTAL, while the inverse (a popover briefly covered) is transient, partial, and outlives the toast. Matches platform convention (toast above popover, below tooltip). NOTE: no doc states a stacking order — this scale is the ONLY authority for it.

shimmer.$description: the skeleton shimmer sweep (D62 UIP-309) — long + calm; reduced-motion drops the animation entirely to a flat muted fill (globals.css .orb-skeleton-shimmer)

breathe.$description: the WeaveGlyph hero shimmer breathing period (client .orb-weave-shimmer) — long + calm, distinct from motion.shimmer (the skeleton sweep); reduced-motion freezes it via the unlayered floor.

precip.$description: the waystone's falling-precipitation loop (globals.css .orb-ws-rain; snow/ash ride multiples of it) — one lattice pitch per cycle, so the fall loops seamlessly. Reduced-motion removes it.

transit.$description: the waystone's STATE-CHANGE transit (sky crossfade, the sun/moon slide along its arc, the hour hand's swing, a weather layer's fade-in) — the living-clock moment after a beat lands. Reduced-motion collapses it via the unlayered floor.

ambient.$description: the waystone's slow sky drift (globals.css .orb-ws-sway / .orb-ws-sway-slow — cloud + fog banks) — long enough to read as weather, never as an animation. Reduced-motion removes it.

usage: Use semantic tokens through @orb/ui/tokens; do not author reusable visual literals in components.
Keep foreground/background pairs together and preserve ThemeScope as the custom-theme boundary.
orb.llm.rules: MUST use a standard DTCG type for portable values. MUST keep runtime CSS expressions in orb.cssValues and explicitly declare whether each output belongs in the Tailwind theme or the generated :root block. NEVER add a custom $type or a second value file.

--orb-density-comfortable-field.description: Stable comfortable-density alias for the field spacing intent. Generated at :root so a nested comfortable scope can restore the canonical value below a compact ancestor without copying a literal into authored CSS.

--orb-density-comfortable-row.description: Stable comfortable-density alias for the row spacing intent.

--orb-density-comfortable-block.description: Stable comfortable-density alias for the block spacing intent.

--orb-density-comfortable-section.description: Stable comfortable-density alias for the section spacing intent.

--orb-density-compact-field.description: Compact-density field spacing, derived from the existing tight step.

--orb-density-compact-row.description: Compact-density row spacing, derived from the existing field step.

--orb-density-compact-block.description: Compact-density block spacing, derived from the existing row step.

--orb-density-compact-section.description: Compact-density section spacing, derived from its canonical portable token because the base scale has no existing 1rem step.

--aspect-portrait.description: the 2:3 VN/portrait avatar aspect (D44/§B.3/§B.4 `FINAL-Persona-and-Immersive-Chat-Visuals.md`) — pairs with the server's smart-cropped `portrait` blob variant (`portraitBlobUrl`). Emits `--aspect-portrait`, driving the core Tailwind v4 `aspect-portrait` utility (the `--aspect-*` theme namespace) — never a raw `aspect-[2/3]` bracket.

--aspect-banner.description: the 3:1 Whisper header-BAND aspect — pairs with the server's smart-cropped 3:1 `blobBannerUrl` variant so the displayed band matches the source crop at ANY bubble width (height DERIVES from width, exactly like `aspect-portrait`). Replaces a fixed band height, which drifted the box aspect off 3:1 as the fluid-width bubble changed and made `background-size:cover` re-crop the already-tight face-safe source. Still a REAL block-level child with a definite box (aspect-ratio gives it height), so text stays in normal flow BELOW it — the Phase-4 anti-squish property is preserved. Emits `--aspect-banner` (the `--aspect-*` theme namespace).

--dimension-panel.description: the LIST side-panel track width (§11.1 clamp-overlay). The CONTEXT panel has its own, wider clamp — see panel-context. This is the IDEAL; at both-docked it is also the pane that gives up the most slack when the content track would drop below dimension.content-reading-floor (#242 — shell.css's squeeze, which never widens it and never takes it below panel-floor).

--dimension-panel-context.description: the CONTEXT side-panel track width (§11.1 clamp-overlay). Wider than the list panel on desktop (owner, 2026-08-01: the rpg takeover was "a bit cramped" once the Waystone grew to its focal 120px). SAME 17rem floor — the responsive floor and the mobile full-width sheet are unchanged; only the desktop ideal/max grew (24vw/26rem -> 30vw/30rem). 30vw, not the first-cut 26vw, is the owner ruling (660b2dd4): a STANDARD 1280px desktop must reach 384px = the 24rem container step where the Waystone paints at its focal 120px — at 26vw that viewport landed on 20.8rem and got the 96px stone. Early design mocks drew 272/340/416px against the old clamp; this widens the ideal, not the grammar.

--reading-measure.description: The transcript's LINE-LENGTH cap — the top of the 65-75ch reading measure, expressed in ch so it tracks the font rather than a viewport guess. The transcript had NO cap (`max-width: none`) and measured 98ch at 1280px with panels closed, ~200ch on a 2560 monitor (side-eye aesthetic shakedown, 2026-08-16, #97). Consumed by globals.css on [data-slot="message-content-column"] as `calc(var(--reading-measure) * var(--reading-body-scale, 1))`, in a column whose own font-size IS the prose font — a ch resolved in the column's unscaled 1rem font rendered ~85 real characters against a 0.9375rem prose line (#213). It caps the CONTENT COLUMN, not the transcript REGION: --width-shell-content (the user's chatWidthPct dial) still owns how wide the thread runs, so the composer and the row gutters keep their geometry and only the line length is bounded.

--reading-measure-min.description: The FLOOR of the same 65-75ch band (#213). `reading.measure` is a MAX with no MIN, so a docked context panel took 177px straight out of the reading column and the line fell to 59ch — the state a reader who keeps Members open lives in permanently. Consumed by globals.css as `min-width: min(100%, calc(var(--reading-measure-min) * var(--reading-body-scale, 1)))`: the `min(100%, …)` half is load-bearing, because a pane can be narrower than the floor itself (measured: a 509px CONTENT pane at list+context docked) and a bare min-width would spill the column out of its pane, which is worse than a short line. Holding the floor in THAT state is a shell-grid question (how narrow a panel may push the content pane), not a transcript one — RULED and BUILT at #242 (dimension.content-reading-floor + shell.css's conditional squeeze), for the REAL-CHARACTER floor: that pane is now 579px and holds 65.1 real characters, while this token's 65 ch (557.7px of prose box) is still unmet there and stays the stated residual.

--tracking-micro.description: letter-spacing for the micro-caps label voice (UIP-103)

--dimension-shell-title-floor.description: The topbar title's six-character visible floor. ch is a CSS-font-relative runtime unit, so the portable source is dimension.shell-title-floor-ch and this is its explicit generated output.

--dimension-shell-notice-cap.description: The shell notice band's normal-flow height budget: the lesser of its portable absolute cap and the current dynamic viewport share. The dvh composition inherently belongs to CSS runtime output.

--shadow-shell-over-art.description: The shell chrome label halo over wallpaper. Its colour must resolve from the active runtime token, so this recipe is explicit CSS output rather than a portable DTCG shadow with a frozen colour.

--shadow-glow.value: 0 0 0 1px oklch(from var(--color-primary) l c h / 0.4), 0 0 18px oklch(from var(--color-primary) l c h / 0.18)
--shadow-glow.description: the ONE rationed accent glow (DESIGN.md §5) — focus/character moment only. It DERIVES from the active theme's --color-primary through the relative-colour form, the same mechanism color.sheen already uses to keep a per-site alpha over a one-decision hue: the old note that per-stop alpha 'must live inside oklch(), so it cannot reference {color.primary}' was a limitation of the plain reference, not of CSS. Why it matters (#232): the glow was the dark Ember literal in EVERY theme, so the Light seed (primary oklch(0.55 0.16 50)) wore the dark ember, and a custom theme's accent never reached its own glow. Relative colour survives Tailwind's build-time inlining of --shadow-* into .shadow-* (probed), so this resolves per theme — including ThemeScope-emitted custom palettes, which no value-set could have covered.

--shadow-overlay.description: modal/popover/card elevation (UIP-401) — a LAYERED float recipe (was the single flat 0 24px 80px drop): a 1px edge-light hairline + an inset top-highlight (the light-from-above cue) + a tight contact shadow + the deep ambient drop. All consumers (card/dialog/popover/menu/tooltip/toast/drawer/command-palette/selection-bar/macro-textarea) inherit it via the shadow-overlay utility. Each stop now names a colour INGREDIENT token instead of a literal (#232), so the recipe's GEOMETRY is one decision here and its polarity is the palette's: the four ingredients are the only part a value-set re-values, and a var() ingredient is the only form that survives Tailwind's build-time inlining of --shadow-* into .shadow-*.

--shadow-cta.description: the primary-CTA static top-highlight (a light-from-above catch on the button's top edge) — a subtle inset white-alpha hairline that reads as a raised, tactile primary button. The catch is the `color.shadow-cta-highlight` ingredient token (#232), so a palette can retune it against its own primary. Consumed as `shadow-cta` on buttonVariants intent:primary; the hover state swaps to `shadow-cta-glow` (this highlight + the rationed Ember glow) so the highlight persists under the hover halo.

--shadow-cta-glow.value: inset 0 1px 0 var(--color-shadow-cta-highlight), 0 0 0 1px oklch(from var(--color-primary) l c h / 0.4), 0 0 18px oklch(from var(--color-primary) l c h / 0.18)
--shadow-cta-glow.description: the primary-CTA HOVER treatment — the `shadow.cta` top-highlight PLUS the one rationed Ember glow (the `shadow.glow` stops, inlined so this is a single box-shadow value that keeps BOTH: a `hover:shadow-glow` alone would drop the highlight). Consumed as `hover:shadow-cta-glow` on buttonVariants intent:primary. Both halves DERIVE (#232): the catch from `color.shadow-cta-highlight`, the two glow stops from the active `--color-primary` through the relative-colour form.
